concepts.def: Three-dimensional work conceived for a specific space, transforming the viewer's experience of that environment.

Work combining multiple materials and techniques, allowing layered meaning and richer visual surfaces.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Mixed Media — a core area of GCSE Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Mixed Media brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Mixed Media.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who created the 'Angel of the North' sculpture installed in 1998?
options: Anish Kapoor
Antony Gormley
Rachel Whiteread
Damien Hirst

mcqs.q: Whose 'Infinity Rooms' are famous immersive installations?
options: Olafur Eliasson
Yayoi Kusama
James Turrell
Cornelia Parker

mcqs.q: What attitude does Pop Art take toward consumer culture?
options: It straightforwardly celebrates capitalism.
He painted indoor scenes.
It rejects all modern imagery.
Ambiguous - it both celebrates and critiques mass media imagery.

mcqs.q: What did Pollock mean by his drip paintings being 'in the painting'?
options: He painted indoor scenes.
He worked from all sides, making the act of painting central to the meaning.
He literally fell into wet paint.
It rejects all modern imagery.

mcqs.q: Why is preserving white in watercolour important?
options: Because white is the most expensive colour.
You can simply paint white over other colours later.
It rejects all modern imagery.
White comes from the paper showing through - there is no true white pigment in traditional watercolour.
